title: Event Hubs Partitions and Consumer Groups
description: Understand how partitions enable parallel processing and how consumer groups isolate read views.

data.text: Partitions are the fundamental scale unit in Event Hubs. Each partition is an ordered log of events. When you send an event, a partition key determines which partition it goes to. Events with the same partition key are guaranteed to be in the same partition and in order.

terms.definition: A value used to assign an event to a partition. Same key = same partition.
A view of an Event Hub. Each consumer group maintains its own offset, so multiple apps can read independently.
A position in a partition stream. Consumers track their offset to know where to resume.
An exclusive ownership mechanism for a partition, ensuring only one consumer reads at a time in a given group.

data.title: Consumer Groups Are Independent
data.text: Each consumer group tracks its own offset. If one consumer group falls behind, it does not affect other groups. Plan consumer groups carefully -- each one increases storage and resource usage.

data.title: Design Consumer Groups for an IoT Solution
data.description: A smart-city IoT platform ingests sensor data into Event Hubs. Plan the consumer groups.
steps: Identify two independent applications that need to read the data.
Name each consumer group and explain why they should be separate.
Decide on a partition key strategy for sensor data.
data.expectedOutcome: Two consumer groups (for example, $Default for real-time dashboards and archive for long-term storage) with a device-ID-based partition key.
